newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce sees Latam trade talks pre-fast track.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce sees Latam trade talks pre-fast track.

text.p: The United States could begin negotiations toward a free trade pact for the Americas before Congress grants the president fast-track authority, Commerce Secretary William Daley said Thursday.
"There's no impediment for us negotiating and beginning serious dialogue on a free trade in the Americas before fast track is passed," Daley said at a press briefing here.

President Bill Clinton met with members of Congress on Wednesday evening to discuss foreign policy issues including fast-track authority to conclude a trade agreement bringing Chile into the North American Free Trade Agreement.
Under fast-track authority, Clinton would be empowered to negotiate a treaty that Congress could either ratify or reject in its entirety, but could not amend.
Daley said he did not expect the administration would unveil its proposed legislation on fast-track authority in the next three weeks.

On an upcoming trip to Latin America, Daley said he would tell policical and business leaders "what we've told them reapeatly: we are committed to relationships, obviously, in the Free Trade in the Americas schedule that was outlined at the summit in Miami in 1995."
